listing_view.reasoning: First-day subscription reached only ~0.40x by mid-afternoon on day one, which is weak retail/QIB mood for a mainboard IPO, and there is no GMP, anchor or broker data to suggest hidden demand. The price-to-latest-EPS of ~22 against a stated benchmark of 45 looks optically cheap, but the document's own weighted EPS is 10.76 (implying ~37x), so the 'cheapness' depends entirely on which earnings you believe.

longterm_view.reasoning: This is a commodity steel roller with 7.3% EBITDA margins, ~3% PAT margins, 4% two-year revenue CAGR and debt exceeding equity, recently levered at 2x+ before the IPO deleverages it. The latest year's profit jump (PAT ₹12.7bn on flat-ish volume economics) came with collapsing operating cash flow (₹32.5bn down to ₹6.3bn of OCF while PAT tripled), so only ~21% of EBITDA converted to cash — that is exactly the pattern of earnings you should distrust in a cyclical at the top.

governance.reasoning: There is a SEBI settlement penalty for regulatory violations, an ROC show-cause for non-disclosure of vigil mechanism, unpaid guarantee fees to promoters, and bank guarantees/loans extended to director-interested related parties (A-One Defence and Aerospace). Individually modest, but the cluster plus a ₹63m GST demand and income-tax assessment under s.153D indicates sloppy compliance in a promoter-heavy company.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Latest-year PAT roughly tripled while operating cash flow fell by more than half, meaning the profit did not arrive as cash — classic working-capital-inflated peak earnings used to price an IPO.

Debt-to-equity was 2.34x two years ago and the document itself states debt ratios will depend on how much of the Net Proceeds is used to repay, so the balance sheet only improves if the issue completes as planned.
The company posted a ₹53.7m bank guarantee for a loan to a director-interested entity and paid no guarantee fees on promoter guarantees, showing cash and credit flowing along promoter channels.
The fresh-issue figure (₹3.55bn) exceeds the computed whole offer (₹2.99bn), so the use-of-proceeds and dilution math cannot be trusted until reconciled by hand against the RHP.

answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: Cannot validate: zero peer rows were parsed, so I cannot say who the peers are or whether the 45.2x benchmark is itself a frothy comp being used to make this issue look cheap. What I can say is the optics are unreliable — at the ₹405 cap the issue is ~22x the flattering latest basic EPS but ~38x the document's own weighted-average EPS of 10.76, so 'cheap vs 45x peers' survives only on one year's peak earnings. Naming a benchmark while leaving the P/E cell blank in the filed document is seller-friendly framing.

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Receivables worsened against the growth claim: latest-year revenue grew 17.1%, but receivable days jumped from ~45-46 to 58.5, i.e. receivables grew materially faster than sales — consistent with pulling revenue forward or loosening credit to show growth. Inventory is not printed in what I was given, but the cash-flow pattern (OCF fell from ₹32.0bn to ₹6.3bn despite PAT tripling) implies the rest of the working-capital build — almost certainly inventory — absorbed a very large sum, which again contradicts the clean profit story.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: If day 2-3 subscription, especially QIB, goes well above 2x with disclosed anchor investors, my listing view rises meaningfully. For the long term, audited FY27 numbers showing operating cash flow back above 70% of EBITDA and receivable days back near 45 would prove the latest year was real turnaround rather than peak-cycle window dressing.
